To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
subliminal singleton onset distractors can capture attention, irrespective of their contrast polarity, and that this capture is not accompanied by an increase in reaction times.

(i) subliminal singleton onset distractors capture attention, (ii) this capture is independent of the contrast polarity of the distractor, (iii) the capture effect can be measured in terms of saccade latency and saccade trajectory, and (iv) the capture effect is stronger when the distractor appears in the opposite field to the target.

subliminal distractor onset in a different hemifield than the target delays saccades to the target, that the effect of subliminal distracters on saccade latencies is independent of the distractor contrast and that the effect of the subliminal distracter onset on the saccade latency is not dependent on the similarity between the target contrast and the distractor contrast.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether oculomotion is controlled by the top-down or by the bottom-up processing stream.
the question of whether the human visual system is able to process information that is presented at a level below the level of conscious awareness.
the role of the stimulus contrast of the distractor in subliminal oculo-motor capture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bottom-up explanation of oculomotor subliminal capture by singleton-onsets is more likely than a top-down explanation.
oculomotor attention is captured by subliminal distractor stimuli in the same way as by supraliminal distractors.
subliminal distractor onset captures attention, and this capture is bottom-up and independent of the contrast polarity of the searched-for target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oculomotor attentional capture by subliminally presented distractors is a bottom-up process, and is independent of the distractors’ contrast polarity.
subliminal ocolomotor capture is not top-down but bottom-up, but that the strength of the capture is dependent on the salience of the distractor.
subliminal distractor capture is a bottom-up phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
subliminal distractor onset can be used as a tool to study bottom-up oculotactic effects.
bottom-up oculotor capture by suprathreshold and subthreshold distractors is similar.
bottom-up oculotomotor capture by a subliminal singleton is possible when the distractor is in the opposite hemifield of the target.
